name: Deafness-oligodontia syndrome
aliases: Syndromic hearing loss with tooth agenesis

criteria.description: Congenital absence of six or more permanent teeth (oligodontia)
Additional dental anomalies such as conical teeth or enamel hypoplasia
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and oligodontia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by family history and genetic testing when available.

imaging: Temporal bone CT or MRI may show cochlear or vestibular anomalies
Dental panoramic radiographs showing missing teeth
genetic: Mutations in the PAX9 gene or MSX1 gene reported in some cases
other: Audiometric testing confirming sensorineural hearing loss
Dental examination confirming oligodontia and tooth morphology anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Skeletal abnormalities with epiphyseal and spinal involvement
Hearing loss and tooth agenesis without other syndromic features
Lack of additional dental anomalies like conical teeth

redFlags: Progressive profound sensorineural hearing loss in early childhood
Multiple missing permanent teeth with abnormal tooth shape
Family history of similar hearing loss and dental anomalies
references: Smith RJH, et al. Syndromic Hearing Loss. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.
